answer: In PoA, identity verification binds each node to a Wesolowski VDF: a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings whose next input depends on the prior result. An attacker simulating many clones must complete a separate chain for every identity; GPUs may add hardware but cannot parallelize each dependency chain, imposing a strict physical time bottleneck. Thus ember, summit, and tide identities cannot be fabricated at scale without proportional elapsed time.
